ev-prambanan:year.reason: The event is the consecration recorded by the Shivagrha inscription, dated Śaka 778 = 12 November 856; Wikidata's c. 850 is the approximate start of construction under Rakai Pikatan. Record medium with note.

ev-fall-of-ayutthaya:coord.reason: The war culminated in the siege and sack of Ayutthaya city (7 April 1767), where the point sits; Wikidata's 13,98.75 is a generic point on the Tenasserim border.

ev-philippine-revolution:coord.reason: Point marks Pugad Lawin/Balintawak (Quezon City), site of the Katipunan's 'Cry' of August 1896; Wikidata's 12,123 is the archipelago centroid.
checked: T. A. Agoncillo, The Revolt of the Masses (1956)

ev-vietnam-war:year.reason: Wikidata's own P580 is 1 November 1955 (US MAAG Vietnam date); the 1975 value is a misused point-in-time. Britannica dates the war 1954–75, within tolerance of 1955.

ev-vietnam-war:coord.reason: Huế, near the 17th-parallel partition and site of the 1968 battle, is a reasonable anchor; Wikidata's 18.2,104.1 lies in Laos. Note added explaining the symbolic placement.

ev-cambodian-genocide:coord.reason: Point is the Choeung Ek killing field outside Phnom Penh, the principal memorial site (noted); Wikidata's 12.25,105.6 is Cambodia's centroid.
checked: B. Kiernan, The Pol Pot Regime (1996)

polity-toungoo:from.reason: Britannica dates the dynasty 1486–1752 (or 1531–1752 from Tabinshwehti); Wikipedia uses 1510, when Toungoo broke with Ava; Wikidata 1485. Record medium; note updated.

ev-nagarakretagama:coord.reason: Wikidata's coordinates are those of the National Library in Jakarta, which holds the manuscript. The record marks the Majapahit court where Prapanca composed it in 1365, at Trowulan, the site generally identified as the capital (BRIN, Berkala Arkeologi).

ev-samudera-pasai-islam:year.reason: The event is the first datable Muslim ruler: Malik al-Salih’s gravestone is dated 696 AH = 1297 CE. Wikidata’s 1267 is the traditional founding date of the Samudra Pasai kingdom, not of this event.
checked: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (2008)

ev-canggal-inscription:coord.reason: Wikidata’s point is the National Museum, Jakarta, where the stone is now kept; the inscription was found on Gunung Wukir, Magelang, Central Java, where the point sits.

ev-pyu-ancient-cities:coord.reason: Wikidata’s point is Halin, one of the three serial sites; the record is pinned at Sri Ksetra, the largest Pyu city (noted in the record).

ev-anawrahta-conquers-thaton:year.reason: Wikidata’s -300 is the legendary start of the Thaton kingdom (its own end date is 17 May 1057); the event is Anawrahta’s conquest of 1057, the chronicle date. Record is low confidence with a note on Aung-Thwin’s critique.
checked: M. Aung-Thwin, The Mists of Rāmañña (2005)

ev-ananda-temple:year.reason: 1105 is the usual completion date (Luce; Wikipedia gives construction c. 1090–1105); Wikidata’s 1091 is the start of construction. Record is medium with a note.

ev-founding-of-lan-xang:coord.reason: Wikidata’s 19,102 is a generic point for the kingdom; Fa Ngum was crowned at Xieng Dong Xieng Thong (Luang Prabang), where the point sits.

ev-le-thanh-tong-conquers-vijaya:coord.reason: Wikidata’s 14,108 is a rounded regional point; the decisive event was the storming of Vijaya (Chà Bàn/Đồ Bàn citadel, Bình Định), where the point sits.

ev-siege-of-batavia:coord.reason: The sieges took place at Batavia (Jakarta); Wikidata’s point lies in Central Java near Mataram’s heartland.

ev-trinh-nguyen-war:coord.reason: The front line ran along the Gianh river and the Nguyễn walls at Đồng Hới (Quảng Bình), where the point sits; Wikidata’s 16,108 is a country-level point.

ev-makassar-war:coord.reason: The point is Somba Opu/Makassar, where the fighting ended in 1669; Wikidata’s -5,120 is a rounded point in South Sulawesi (70 km).
checked: L. Y. Andaya, The Heritage of Arung Palakka (1981)

ev-nguyen-dynasty-founded:coord.reason: The QID is the dynasty, whose Wikidata point (16,108) is a country centroid; the founding is placed at Huế (Phú Xuân), the capital.

ev-first-anglo-burmese-war:coord.reason: British forces opened the main campaign by landing at Rangoon in May 1824 (the record also carries a route to Yandabo); Wikidata’s 22,96 is a generic point for Burma.

ev-anglo-dutch-treaty-1824:coord.reason: Signed in London (Wikidata), but the atlas places treaties where they took effect; the point marks the Strait of Malacca, the line the treaty drew. Noted in the record.

ev-aceh-war:coord.reason: The war began with the 1873 landings at Kutaraja (Banda Aceh), seat of the sultanate; Wikidata’s point is in central Aceh.

ev-franco-siamese-crisis:coord.reason: Wikidata’s point is Hanoi; the crisis came to a head at the Paknam forts at the mouth of the Chao Phraya (13 July 1893), where the point sits.

ev-malayan-emergency:coord.reason: The point is Sungai Siput, Perak, where the killing of three planters on 16 June 1948 led to the emergency (noted); Wikidata’s 7,100 is in southern Thailand.

ev-singapore-independence:coord.reason: The agreement was signed in Kuala Lumpur (Wikidata), but independence was proclaimed and took effect in Singapore on 9 August 1965.

ev-indonesian-mass-killings:coord.reason: Wikidata’s -2,118 is Indonesia’s centroid; the record is pinned in Central Java, one of the worst-affected regions with East Java and Bali (noted).

ev-laotian-civil-war:coord.reason: Wikidata’s point is Vientiane; the record marks the Plain of Jars, the main battleground of the war (noted).

ev-cambodian-vietnamese-war:year.reason: Wikidata’s point in time 1989 is the withdrawal; its own start is 30 April 1977 (border clashes). The record dates the full invasion of 25 December 1978 and notes the 1977 clashes.

ev-cambodian-vietnamese-war:endYear.reason: Vietnamese troops completed their withdrawal in September 1989; Wikidata’s 1991 is the Paris Peace Agreements, which ended the wider conflict.

ev-cambodian-vietnamese-war:coord.reason: The decisive event was the capture of Phnom Penh on 7 January 1979; Wikidata’s 12.5,105 is Cambodia’s centroid.
